headline: Bitcoin is holding near $65,000 in Asian trading on Monday after its weekend drop to about $62,000, with fear still extreme and futures traders now pricing a roughly 94-95% chance of a December Fed rate hike.

market.asOf: Read at about 04:00 UTC Mon 16 Nov (11:00 Bangkok) from CoinGecko coin pages; CoinMarketCap and Alternative.me could not be opened this run. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: CoinGecko's Fear & Greed gauge read 19 out of 100 (Extreme Fear) on its homepage and 21 on its bitcoin page at about 04:00 UTC; KuCoin's daily report put Fear & Greed at 10 as of 00:00 UTC.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $65,000 in Asia after a weekend low near $62,000
stories.summary: Bitcoin bounced from its weekend low and was trading around $65,000 in the Asian session on Monday, while Asian stock markets fell. The weekend drop forced out more than $2B of borrowed bets, most of them bets on higher prices. Ether and Solana fell harder than bitcoin over the week.
points: Bitcoin was at $65,206 at 9:27pm ET Sunday (02:27 UTC Monday), per TokenPost, which also said the MSCI Asia-Pacific index fell more than 1% and South Korean tech-heavy indexes more than 3%.
The weekend low was $61,946 on Coinbase, per CryptoTicker; Cointelegraph gave a 24-hour low of $62,080.91 using CoinGecko data.
The weekly fall was 14.2% to $64,910 by late Sunday afternoon, per The Block; Cointelegraph's weekly roundup had a 12.4% loss at $65,116.
About $2.02B of crypto bets were force-closed (liquidated) from 8am ET Saturday to 8am ET Sunday, $1.68B of them bets on higher prices, per The Block.
Ether fell 18.2% on the week to $1,815 and Solana 19.7% to $71.68, per The Block; ether's low was $1,715 at 01:45 UTC on 15 November, per CryptoTicker.

sources.label: TokenPost: Monday price and Asian stocks
The Block: weekly fall and liquidations

stories.title: Fed hike odds climb to about 94-95% as money keeps leaving crypto funds
stories.summary: Futures traders now see a December interest-rate rise by the Fed as very likely; that is a market bet, not a Fed decision, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks later today. US bitcoin and ether funds have been losing money for weeks, and the supply of the big dollar stablecoins is shrinking.
points: Markets price a 94% chance of a 0.25-point hike in December and a 6% chance of a 0.5-point move, per Business Recorder; KuCoin, citing CME FedWatch, put the 0.25-point odds at 95%, up from 88.5% on Saturday per CryptoTicker.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.07B last week, $1.91B over a seven-day outflow streak since 5 November and $2.35B over two weeks, per The Block; BlackRock's IBIT lost $143.5M on Friday.
US ether ETFs lost $398.9M, their seventh straight week of withdrawals, per The Block.

Stablecoin supply fell $17B over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022, leaving USDT and USDC at $244B, their lowest since September 2025, per Glassnode data cited by CoinDesk; Coinbase Institutional counted a record $11.5B fall for USDT, USDC and DAI in 30 days, per CryptoTicker.

stories.title: Bitcoin-holding companies under pressure: Saylor hints at a buy, Metaplanet books a loss, MSCI removals near
stories.summary: Strategy chairman Michael Saylor posted a hint of another bitcoin purchase, but nothing is confirmed until the company discloses a buy. Strategy's bitcoin is worth less than it paid. Japan's Metaplanet reported a loss after selling bitcoin, and both companies leave MSCI indexes after 30 November.
points: Saylor posted "This dip could use a little orange"; Strategy holds 850,364 BTC at an average cost of $75,456, an implied paper loss of about $8.46B (a tracker showed $8.69B), per Bitcoin.com News.
MSCI is removing Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi at the 30 November close, and JPMorgan estimated about $2.8B of selling pressure from Strategy's removal alone, per Cointelegraph.
Metaplanet reported a nine-month net loss of 27.16 billion yen (about $170M), including a 19.17 billion yen loss on selling 10,000 BTC; it held 44,000 BTC at the end of September, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Kava Lend exploited
briefs.summary: An attacker borrowed about 55.2M KAVA, worth about $3.76M before the attack, on 14 November; Upbit, Bithumb and Coinone paused KAVA deposits and withdrawals, KAVA fell about 39% to $0.042, and 612,416 USDT was blocked at a bridge, per FinanceFeeds.

briefs.title: Bitcoin mining machines hijacked, but no block mined
briefs.summary: About 64,000 machines with about 13 EH/s of mining power were redirected to the OCEAN pool with payouts to an attacker; the attack stopped before any block was found, per TokenPost.

briefs.title: Wallet linked to the Ethereum Foundation sells 7,500 ETH
briefs.summary: A wallet that Lookonchain links to the Ethereum Foundation sold 7,500 ETH (about $14.52M) over four days; ownership is not confirmed, per Analytics Insight.

briefs.title: Zcash dev-fund vote opens today
briefs.summary: The Zcash Community Grants vote runs 16-30 November; ZEC was $892.80 on 14 November after a 30.5% weekly drop, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: US regulators sue Arkansas over prediction markets
briefs.summary: The Justice Department and CFTC sued Arkansas on 12 November to stop its case against Kalshi, the 11th state the CFTC has sued, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: XRP hits its lowest since November 2024
briefs.summary: XRP fell to a low of 89 cents, and US XRP ETFs had a $19.13M weekly outflow, their largest since March, per CoinDesk citing SoSoValue.

briefs.title: MegaETH cuts staff
briefs.summary: MegaETH reduced its workforce by 20% and committed $30M to AI products, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Senate hearing on two SEC nominees on Thursday
briefs.summary: The Senate Banking Committee holds a nomination hearing on 19 November at 10am ET, including SEC nominees Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine, per the committee.
